answers.implementation_then_now: Implementation does not apply on either date because the protection answer is the lowest option. Lawfully present foreigners had no vote in 2023 and still had none in 2026. Under Constitution arts. 19, 90 and 93, suffrage belongs to citizens, and citizens are Costa Ricans. In the window, no reform, ruling or practice was found that let resident foreigners vote, including in municipal elections. The 2024 municipal and 2026 national elections were held under the same rules.
answers.sourcing_note: I read the current SINALEVI consolidated Constitution, whose amendment notes appear under each article. The latest notes are art. 90 (Ley 4763, 1971) and art. 93 (Ley 2345, 1959); arts. 19 and 94 carry no amendment note. So the 2023 text is the same as today's. The TSE Revista de Derecho Electoral PDFs (Bonilla Bravo; Blanco Gamboa, who proposes reforming art. 19) could not be read because the PDF tool failed.

answers.notes: Decisive passages, in Spanish: art. 19 'No pueden intervenir en los asuntos políticos del país'; art. 90 'La ciudadanía es el conjunto de derechos y deberes políticos que corresponden a los costarricenses mayores de dieciocho años'; art. 93 'por los ciudadanos inscritos en el Registro Civil'. The academic reform proposals in the TSE journal were found only through search results; no bill adopted in the window was identified. The Electoral Code (Ley 8765) was not read.

answers.implementation_then_now: Implementation does not apply on either date because the protection answer is the lowest option. On both dates, every elected national and municipal office required Costa Rican nationality and active citizenship: deputy (Const. art. 108), President (art. 131), mayor (Código Municipal art. 15), councillor (art. 22) and district council member (art. 56). No practice shift was found.
answers.sourcing_note: I read the consolidated Constitution and Municipal Code on SINALEVI, with amendment notes per article. Art. 22 was last reformed by Ley 9436 (2017). Arts. 15, 56, 108 and 131 carry no amendment note. The nearby art. 14 bis was reformed by Ley 10547 (Oct. 2024), but that change concerns vice-mayors and not nationality requirements. So the 2023 text matches today's. The TSE PDF of the Municipal Code cited in the starting answer could not be read (PDF tool failure); the SCIJ consolidation was read instead.

sources_opened.title: Constitución Política de la República de Costa Rica (SINALEVI consolidated, arts. 19, 108, 131)

answers.notes: Decisive passages, in Spanish: Código Municipal art. 15 'a) Ser costarricense y ciudadano en ejercicio'; art. 22 'a) Ser ciudadano en ejercicio y costarricense ... d) Estar inscrito como elector en el cantón que corresponda'; art. 56 applies the art. 22 requirements to district council members. Const. art. 108: 'Ser costarricense por nacimiento, o por naturalización con diez años de residencia'; art. 131: 'Ser costarricense por nacimiento y ciudadano en ejercicio'.
